# Project Angerona (AngeronaSuite) - llms.txt

Version: 1.15.1
Date: 2026-11-13
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite

## LATEST (v1.15.1 — security maintenance and watchdog modes)

- The PC source checkout is the authoritative maintenance copy; GitHub receives
  its exact reviewed commit through the guarded publisher. Read the 1.15.1
  version notes and dated worklist report for scope and remaining gaps.
- Optional unsigned third-watchdog monitoring is OFF by default. It is an
  ordinary-user reduced-protection mode with real generation-bound progress,
  no privileged service/firewall/containment authority and explicit recovery
  availability limits. The current helper shares the Core job lifetime and
  reports independent recovery unavailable. It never supplies installed
  Protect authority.
- Installed/SCM supervision requires native own-image signature verification
  and protected final-byte/certificate enrollment before private authority
  reads, writes or service dispatch. Signing alone is insufficient.
- The third-watchdog signature marker is separate from its EKG: green check
  only for verified exact-image signature metadata, red cross for unsigned or
  unverified. Clicking it opens Watchdog signing settings. A stale signed
  process still flatlines; PID presence is not heartbeat proof.
- Selected signed files are inspected as data by the reviewed helper, never
  executed. Signing-update requests are explicitly UNTRUSTED; a separately
  governed installer must reverify and apply enrollment. Source UI never
  elevates mutable checkout code or imports certificates/trust roots.
- Unknown native retirement retains provider/file owners under a sticky custody
  hold, refuses later native admission and never retries an uncertain close.
  Optional observer source admission streams at most 256 directory entries,
  at most 128 recorded inputs, 2 MiB per source and a 32 MiB image, with a
  five-second checked budget between steps. This is not OS-call cancellation.
- A real successfully signed/enrolled positive deployment remains unaccepted;
  mocks and unsigned native fixtures cannot establish that case. The readable
  manual introduces current 1.15.1 source companions; Word/PDF remains the
  older 1.15.0 / 9 November edition, with its original body and dated evidence.
- Optional monitor startup uses a single-use Event; native work is admitted only
  after Thread.start returns successfully. Unknown start stays sticky-held while
  other Core workers continue. Scanner GUI quit is queued only after authenticated
  STOP and successful cleanup. Maintenance ownership accepts at most 16 harmless
  Python prefix switches and rejects -c/unknown-entry confusion.
- AI provider self-test explanations are clearer, but required per-machine write
  custody that is unverified remains FAIL. A read-only host assessment confirmed
  that uncertainty; no malware/compromise verdict or ACL rewrite follows.
- Scheduled-task comparisons ignore only distinct Ready/Running/Queued states
  when all strictly validated selected fields match. Other definition changes,
  disabled/unknown states, incomplete records and duplicate identities remain
  drift or unknown. Raw snapshots, baselines and alerts are unchanged. The
  focused source/baseline cohort passed 164 cases; this is not whole-task-XML
  coverage or a trust grant for any named application.
- Windows native private-file renames include an explicit UTF-16 terminator
  inside the supplied buffer while preserving counted filenames, native errno
  identity, ACLs and retained-handle publication. The old encoding reproduced
  16 invalid-name failures versus 16 terminated successes. The final native
  suite passed 93 top-level tests with one explicit skip and Go vet; the dated
  acceptance note separately retains a budget-incomplete extended stress scope.
- Accepted scoped maintenance gates and the actual ordinary-user diagnostic
  observer/unsigned-inspection exercise are recorded in
  analysis/maintenance-v1.15.1-acceptance-2026-11-13.md. The endpoint was a
  diagnostic Core only. Final syntax/selfcheck/provider/interoperability,
  publication and hosted receipts retain separate result slots.
- Earlier 1.15.0 validation and deployed-authority limits below remain dated
  evidence; no new hosted success or live coverage follows from those records.

- Current FIM root coverage/deadline fields are validated symmetrically at
  native receipt issuance and historical verification, preserving exact lease,
  object, generation, caller and signature admission. Mobile CLI failures retain
  their health score beside authorization holds. Watchdog contextual help now
  matches its Settings controls. Hosted fixture reconciliation retains native
  durable-replay checks and honest Windows deception creation holds.

- Known FIM and zero-trust network collection gaps keep their original HIGH
  warnings but use closed, typed producer envelopes for health classification.
  A filename or free-text lifecycle phrase cannot downgrade genuine findings.
  Only current BaseModule crash/quarantine envelopes gain lifecycle health;
  unfamiliar formats retain ordinary conservative classification. Actual file,
  DNS/DHCP and critical gateway changes still use their independent rules.
- Held STOP feedback distinguishes unavailable authorization from assumed UAC
  refusal and makes no continuing-protection claim. Protected STOP authority,
  source elevation refusal, alerts, baselines and response gates are unchanged.
- The 86aa hosted Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13 matrices passed 17,721 cases with 54
  skips each. Python 3.12 reached 16,103 passes/52 skips with no failed cases
  before its 60-minute job budget; it was interrupted, not accepted as green.
  All Python lanes now have the same finite 75-minute budget. New-head hosted
  checks and fresh changed-source observation retain separate receipts.

## CURRENT REVIEW (v1.15.1 — 13 November security candidate)

- Version 1.15.1 integrates the reviewed worklist candidate, initially based on
  commit 3291279, with authoritative PC baseline fd378df and the signing/mode
  changes. Prior checks do not establish exact-commit live acceptance or new
  green hosted checks. Read
  `docs/releases/security-worklist-review-2026-11-13.md`,
  `analysis/security-worklist-progress-2026-11-13.md` and the scoped independent
  source audit before interpreting earlier completion statements.
- Recovery now has 55 exact members in the builder, PowerShell verifier and
  application literal profile; CI and publisher require all three plus the
  manifest and four unique batch pins to agree. Canonical source startup uses
  a fresh private bytecode prefix before helper import. Earlier 48-member
  historical records below do not describe this candidate.
- Source ZIP staging reconstructs Git subtree IDs and requires the exact file
  set and blob hashes. Managed-lineage evidence holds automatic historical-HEAD
  rollback, and unattended GitHub-parent fallback was removed. Canonical GitHub
  remains the supplier; independent signing, runtime generation freshness and
  direct-target current-main proof are not implemented.
- Local authority checks use fixed KnownFolder paths, owner/DACL/ancestry custody
  and ACL-before-key publication. Stopped heartbeat flags alone cannot grant
  stand-down. Restart claims have bounded freshness and consumed nonces. Corrupt
  bookkeeping and ring headers have bounded degraded recovery paths; unknown
  native process custody never authorizes termination. Outboxes use verified
  peek, accepted EventBus publish, then exact ACK; observations grant no response.
- Mobile self/health/review feedback is filtered before authentication and token
  allocation. Protected-store-only 6–12-digit PIN state uses cumulative durable
  attempt charges, backoff and local rearm after ten failures. Nonces/tokens burn
  before comparison. Signal identity-key proof and whole-store freshness remain open.
- Engine protocol v2 uses mutual role-separated proof, 8 pre-auth slots with one
  absolute 1-second deadline and 4 separate dispatch slots. Exact close ownership
  is atomic. AUTH codec checks do not certify live routing. Mail has verified TLS,
  bounded I/O and in-memory delivered-message dedup; observations remain advisory.
  ACKs are authenticated, exact and expiring; process suppression requires authenticated
  target/digest policy. Legacy broad rows cannot become suppression authority.
  Reviewed feed/model UI is literal/escaped.
- Ollama admission has bounded protected-package/DLL custody, fixed-local model
  path checks and machine-context signing-chain/root checks. Legacy broad-kill,
  download/install/persistence helpers are retired. Writable per-user installs
  may be held; no ACL rewrite, invented publisher fingerprint, actual vendor-PKI
  acceptance or lifetime model-root lease is claimed. Foreign/shared daemon
  image identity does not prove its model/cloud/environment settings.
- Deliberate unavailable capabilities: POSIX automatic binary installation holds
  before mutation; reviewed source setup remains separate. All new Windows legacy
  deception mutations hold before effect pending an object-relative provider.
  Existing exact static canaries retain read-only monitoring. Typed Windows hold
  is SKIP, never PASS; genuine contract, crash, timeout and worker failures stay FAIL.
  Dormant syscall-bridge setup exits before packaging helpers and its C file
  rejects direct compilation;32 entry/fallback-boundary cases passed. The
  historical native algorithms remain uncorrected, uncompiled and unadmitted.
- Live Debug adds bounded advisory OS client-PID audit with explicit loss; no
  image/birth/trust or response inference. Same-SID readers, fairness and best-effort
  free-text confidentiality remain limits. FIM admits covered roots independently
  and binds stat cache to the verified baseline digest. Process Monitor retires
  PID-only startup suppression after fresh valid-count inventory. Memory region
  classification masks the base protection byte, retaining full raw flags in
  evidence/repeat identity; 126 regression cases passed. No new traversal, native
  payload read or response authority follows from that metadata check.
- Scoped gates include 332 Ollama fake-boundary cases plus 2 private native leases,
  134 self-test precedence cases and 26 callable-integrity cases. The source report
  lists the other overlapping cohorts; do not sum them into a suite total. Broad
  activation/coherence attempts exceeded diagnostic budgets and are not green.
  Two representative real-flush cases passed; no production durability was removed.
  Final trusted-path WLAN fixtures passed 16 cases. Offscreen selfcheck passed all 29
  phases, with 70 module PASS/16 module SKIP across 86 modules plus one pipeline PASS.
  Thirteen widget owners, 13 readers and eight Python workers retired; Qt closed.
  The 30-step inert Red Team fixture is not live detector/containment evidence.
  Whole-source syntax 1655 verified; late WLAN files compiled in their gates.
  Fresh runtime acceptance remains pending.
- Original native Go test image passed 63 top-level cases with 1 export-only skip
  locally and on a verified real C-drive short alias, unchanged source/image.
  The empty owned C fixture was removed after closed custody. Hosted missing-spawnlock failure remains
  unexplained. All Python matrix jobs now request pinned Go 1.27.4, pending hosted CI.
- Source-profile same-user keys, whole-root rollback, administrator/kernel tampering,
  production PPL/ELAM/WDAC, optional native driver defects and Source Observe
  network enforcement remain outside the established protection boundary. The native
  syscall bridge is already hard-held with degraded health 55; its fallback self-test
  is descriptive, not operation efficacy proof. Dormant C defects remain unpatched.
  No real UAC/firewall/service/driver activation, Signal send, operator-secret
  access or Ollama provider launch/stop/download occurred in these review gates.

## WINDOWS SERVICE PREPARATION (2026-11-13 — not deployed)

- The native watchdog now has an exclusive `--service` entry for SCM name
  `AngeronaWatchdog3`. It proves its actual own-process SYSTEM/Session-0
  registration, exact image/arguments, type-0 SID policy and protected image
  custody before running the existing guarded supervisor. SCM running means
  dispatcher responsiveness, never engine sensor health. Stop/shutdown cancels
  and awaits the actual supervisor return; console service entry has no fallback.
- The engine remains `AngeronaProtection`, `NT SERVICE\AngeronaProtection`,
  restricted service SID type 3. Its package/token/process/state guards are
  unchanged. MSIX desktop6:Service's built-in account choices cannot represent
  this profile. A separately governed installer and actual signed-package VM
  acceptance remain missing; registration or a publisher certificate alone
  would not close that gap. No host service, task, trust or key was provisioned.
- `tools/Get-AngeronaServiceReadiness.ps1 -AsJson` reports read-only bounded
  observations and always leaves activation unverified. It does not execute a
  candidate, elevate, inspect secret bytes or modify native state. Local cert
  absence does not exclude external HSM/cloud signing.
- `tools/prepare_windows_service_request.py` writes a canonical, explicitly
  UNTRUSTED planning request for a supplied source commit, never runtime config
  or an installer. It cannot enroll publisher/package pins, create keys, sign
  or install. The release workflow's external-authority stop gate stays intact.
- Publisher enrollment, final-signing order and deployment acceptance steps:
  `docs/enterprise/WINDOWS_SERVICE_ONBOARDING.md`. Public trust signing needs
  account-owner identity verification; no development self-signing workaround
  or exportable CI signing secret has been introduced.
- Final Windows checks: full native Go suite and go vet passed; 130 selected
  Python/installer/policy/interoperability cases passed, one directory-symlink
  case skipped because creation was unavailable. The rebuilt unsigned native
  executable exited zero for --version, refused console --service with exit 1
  and missing installed configuration with exit 3; all probe generations
  retired. No watchdog config directory or service installation was created.

## NATIVE THIRD WATCHDOG (2026-11-13 — Go development build)

- New standalone Windows amd64 module: `frz/watchdog3/`. Build with
  `tools/Build-AngeronaWatchdog3.ps1`; default artifact is
  `build/watchdog3/watchdog3.exe`, plus input hashes and third-party notices.
  Go 1.27.4 is pinned in CI; CGO is disabled. This executable does not need
  Python. Development artifacts are unsigned and have not been registered or
  activated on this host. No certificate or service authority was created.
- IMPORTANT: the historical pair-based outline is not the installed contract.
  Frozen `Angerona.exe --chill` is rejected. The admitted SCM service uses
  exactly `Angerona.exe --engine-service`, restricted virtual account
  `NT SERVICE\AngeronaProtection`, own-process registration and its existing
  package/service/token/storage guards. That graph intentionally does NOT run
  ResilienceManager or publish the legacy core/watchdog heartbeat pair. The
  native implementation therefore uses fixed-service SCM observations and
  StartService, without fabricating heartbeat progress or relaxing those guards.
- Schema 2 has exactly six fields: schema, data_dir, launcher_path,
  launcher_sha256, launcher_args (exactly ["--engine-service"]),
  working_directory. The fixed config is the native ProgramData known folder's
  `Angerona/watchdog3/config.json`, controlled by Administrators/SYSTEM.
  data_dir is this supervisor's own separately provisioned private authority
  and runtime namespace, NOT the service's `Protection` root or ambient Core
  data. Keys are never created/repaired by the supervisor.
- Clean SCM Win32ExitCode zero never authorizes a restart, including stale
  ServiceExitCode values. Only failed stopped services can recover after
  180-second startup and continuous 20-second failure grace. Pending, paused,
  running or uncertain ownership prevents duplicate starts. Signed STOP,
  registration, process generation, image custody and authenticated ledger
  are checked again at dispatch. No service install/change/stop or process
  termination, hidden persistence or owner-termination resistance exists.
- Restart pressure survives supervisor restarts; retry backoff caps at 60s
  without permanent give-up. Outbox exhaustion/tamper is an explicit evidence
  gap, not automatic recovery authority and not a permanent recovery block.
  Unknown file/native/SCM resource closes propagate and hold future allocation.
- Optional Python admission/observation adapters are in
  `resilience/native_watchdog.py`; manager/status presentation uses cached
  observations and an independent alert cursor, never source autostart or
  proof of service liveness. Signing must precede pinning final bytes in
  WATCHDOG3_SHA256/WATCHDOG3_PUBLISHER; public unsigned requests leave pins empty.
  Installer registration must survive either Python process's child Job.
- Current validation: Go 63 top-level tests plus their subtests, one opt-in
  exporter skip; go vet and legacy Go console/STOP cases passed. The compiled
  native --version check exited zero without Python on PATH/PYTHONHOME.
  Schema-2 Python integration and actual frozen-entry fixtures passed 74 cases.
  The separate interoperability/recovery/release-policy run passed 147 cases
  in 193.99s, exit zero with completed unconfigure and Python exit. The full
  16,304-case suite was not repeated for this change.
  Native SCM tests were injected, and native process tests used owned inert
  helpers. No live Angerona/service activation or provisioning was performed.
- The existing source recovery profile stays operational48/v1: the new
  Python adapter is optional/lazy/caught as unavailable, not a recovery-startup
  dependency. Changed manager bytes and both launcher pins were regenerated.
  Private analyses, raw host/test logs and the full handoff remain outside git.

  unique passing focused cases. Scoped Ruff 0.16.0, all 48 recovery-manifest
  entries, both launcher pins and documentation drift passed.
- Full Windows/Python 3.12.10 run: 16,234 passed, 68 skipped, two failed
  (16,304 collected; exit 1; normal unconfigure and Python exit completed).
  The native beacon fixture read an exclusively created output before its
  synchronous writer closed it. Both positive tests now wait for verified
  watcher retirement before parsing, retaining every original assertion.
  The other failure was a 60-second PowerShell diagnostic-fixture timeout;
  its test and production helpers are unchanged from `df4e9e6`. Concurrent
  read-only PowerShell delays were observed, without a proven root cause.
  The full beacon file and exact unchanged PowerShell test passed together
  afterwards: 71 cases, exit 0, with completed unconfigure and Python exit.
  The full suite was not repeated after the beacon fixture-only change.
- The previously failing base-CI Python 3.13 native Ollama retirement case
  passed here on 3.12. This does not establish 3.10/3.13 compatibility or
  replace those dated CI failures with a green result.
- No live Angerona restart, elevated path, STOP provisioning, AutoLogger
  apply or real firewall change was performed. The third Go watchdog
  was still an unbuilt outline at that point. Earlier live-triage observations below remain
  dated findings and are not superseded by this offline validation.

## PENDING (2026-11-11 restart-loop / STOP hardening — branch `hardening/restart-loop-stop-authority`)

- The ranked attack-path analysis for this pass is a local-only file
  (`analysis/hardening-v1.15-2026-11-11-exploit-analysis.md`, excluded from
  git, not published). Ask the operator for it before changing these controls.
- Test drift fixed (full run 16,129 pass / 31 fail / 1 error before fixes):
  Red Team preflight tests use 3x60 s (serial probe time keeps the 4,500 s
  hard limit), the journal test binds the admitted TTL, the live GUI spy
  matches the isolated `-I -S` probe argv, launcher tests use an absolute
  path (`NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath`), autonomy fakes accept
  `action=`. 19 startup-repair failures were host disk space (<5 GiB on D:).
- `resilience/peer_alerts.py`: peer watchdog supervisor events (MEDIUM+) go
  to an HMAC-chained outbox the core drains (`manager._drain_peer_alerts`);
  the core-death alert was previously dropped (`watchdog.py` had no
  `on_event`).
- `resilience/control_authority.py`: once provisioned (elevated, one time),
  STOP/RESUME are Ed25519-signed in `<ProgramData>\Angerona\control`
  (Admins/SYSTEM write, Users list/read), epoch-bound so RESUME retires
  captured STOPs; UAC via `request_elevated`; frozen entry
  `--control-authority`. `shutdown_token` refuses the legacy user-dir HMAC
  stand-down when provisioned; unprovisioned hosts keep the legacy contract.
- `resilience/supervisor.py` restart ledger: unexpected stops counted over
  10 min/1 h/24 h (persisted in `recovery_state` `pressure`); escalates
  High "elevated" / Critical "attack"; under attack SAFE_MODE cools down in
  15 s; relaunched core gets `ANGERONA_RECOVERY_PRESSURE` and
  `module_manager` starts Process Monitor, Persistence Sweep and FIM
  immediately with a 5 s staged-cycle cap. Each relaunch emits a MEDIUM
  coverage-gap lower bound.
- `core/service_recovery.py`: installer step for SCM failure actions on
  `AngeronaProtection` (restart 5 s/5 s/30 s, 24 h reset, non-crash
  failures) plus read-only `verify()`. Logon tasks now use RestartCount 999.
- Follow-up 2026-11-12 (Windows offline results recorded above): `core/privilege.py` now
  carries `ANGERONA_RECOVERY_PRESSURE` through the sidecar environment
  allow-list; before this the hint was dropped and priority-sensor relaunch
  never triggered outside tests. The crash sweep treats junctions and other
  reparse points as links. The startup-recovery manifest and both
  `start-angerona.bat` pins were regenerated: the hardening commit changed
  six pinned files without doing so, so the source launcher's verifier saw
  them as drift. Repeat that step after any change to a pinned file.
- At the original restart-loop review the third non-Python watchdog was only
  an outline. Its later Go/SCM implementation and unsigned deployment status
  are recorded above; do not confuse it with the legacy Go parent.
  Original design: `frz/THIRD_WATCHDOG_OUTLINE.md`.
  Coverage for the pair-kill gap comes from SCM recovery (signed package),
  the Task Scheduler backstop and the restart ledger. The existing Go parent
  in `frz/` remains unbuilt and carries the defects listed in the analysis.
- `resilience/crash_hunter.py`: on an unexpected core stop the peer watchdog
  runs one bounded READ-ONLY sweep (new processes, their remote endpoints,
  recent temp drops, Run/RunOnce digest), at most once per 60 s; report in
  the diagnostics folder plus an outbox alert. It changes nothing and cannot
  identify who stopped the core.
- `resilience/deadman.py`: OFF by default. With an administrator-signed
  policy (`control_authority.set_deadman`, 120-3600 s) an ELEVATED watchdog
  adds two fixed firewall block rules (`Angerona-DeadMan-out/-in`) after the
  core stays down past the threshold, verifies them by readback, rolls back
  on partial apply and releases 15 s after the core returns or on stand-down.
  Unelevated: reports once, never acts. Fake-firewall tests only; NEVER run
  against the real firewall.
- `tools/Stage-AngeronaAutoLogger.ps1`: dry-run by default; elevated
  `-Apply` registers a circular 64 MB Kernel-Process AutoLogger
  (`AngeronaBoot`), `-Remove` deletes it. Never applied. Angerona does NOT
  read the .etl yet (no replay-on-start).
- UI: Watchdog monitor (`resilience/status_ui.py`) has a Protection group
  (`resilience/posture.py`: STOP protection, restart pressure, network hold,
  Windows service recovery) with a one-time "Require administrator approval
  for STOP" button; the Details row is readable text.
- Validation so far: full local suite on 46d3ff0 (2026-11-12): 16,200 pass,
  84 skip, 5 fail, 1 error; the six are host-dependent (temp-directory
  access-denied, process churn, worktree path) and reproduce on unchanged
  code or pass on rerun. No live-host run, no elevated path exercised, STOP authority not provisioned on this host.

- Final staging-only format qualifier: one surplus EOF blank line was removed
  from each of two newly staged community-tool tests. ASTs including line
  attributes are unchanged; two in-memory compiles and scoped Ruff passed,
  without PYC. The full 1,581-file/27,924,607-byte/3c697a67 snapshot below is a
  dated pre-format gate. Final content fingerprint only:1,581files/27,924,605B,
  62f4cb27d975454a79179fafe4f2dd995397a7078161017a25006f01caaca4d4;
  1,579files remain byte-identical. This is not a repeated full gate. Product
  code, media and Word are unchanged; the earlier missing-Ruff-path harness
  attempt remains retained.
- Final integrated caption/idle follow-up: header text uses ceiling-rounded
  fractional spans after polish; a complete styled allocation keeps the full
  semantic label, while true underallocation still elides. Known ready/idle
  dedicated Spyware controls without bound request evidence show the selected
  next-run budget, not generic status-operation timing. Existing summary signal
  refreshes it; bound/active/completed/held/partial/unknown/standalone timing and
  cancellation stay unchanged. Private header81/81 and scan64/64 passed; the
  post-integration tracked normal-import30/30 gate passed (15caption+15timing).
  All overlap other cohorts and are not a unique total or production pixel proof.

- Later alerts/Red Team source follow-up: alert sizing coalesces native resize/style

  terminal/stop context now survives writer-first shutdown. Nonempty history

  Sanitized follow-up: analysis/hardening-v1.15-2026-10-30-followup.md. Final fresh
  post-remediation lifecycle result is recorded separately below.
- Final changed-source Full 120s/STOP lifecycle accepted:true: native Core exit 0,

## Historical v1.14.2 — curated tools, priority scans and breach review

- Source/application version is 1.14.2; Windows package metadata derives 1.14.2.0.
  Component implementation versions remain independent. Broader 1.15 is still
  incomplete. This source publication is not an accepted signed release; the
  external signing authority remains unprovisioned. Current validation and
  limitations are recorded in analysis/curated-tools-breach-2026-10-29.md and
  docs/releases/v1.14.2.md. Historical observations below keep their dated scope.
- GitHub Tools and SpywareGuard's native Zero Breach tab share one curated-tool
  controller and managed job state. The full 968987-byte Zero Breach 0.1.10 engine
  is pinned at 81bd556ba604685dbd1c0ecb48138c10f43cccf8 with SHA256
  075b2a0ac20f285fa4385d6b6c5cda2cedd410364c4f4686db3c1b8b033265d3.
  Standard-library preparation adds no pip dependencies. Retain Apache-2.0
  LICENSE/NOTICE, CC0 indicator attribution and Candiru DRL-1.1/CC-BY-SA 4.0
  notices, including MSTIC and Felix Bilstein credits. Angerona's MIT license
  does not replace those terms. See docs/zero-breach-toolkit.md.
- Third-party scanning runs only in a separate owned ordinary-user source
  process. Never import the engine into Core/GUI: upstream socket globals are
  modified inside its interpreter. Installed/elevated execution is HELD pending
  an accepted ordinary-user broker. The Source Library stays a data-only ZIP
  review workflow; existing Analysis Lab acceptance holds remain unchanged.
- Native modes are default/full/browser/targeted plus explicit local phone
  backup/filesystem/sysdiagnose inputs, quick/preview, local indicators and
  existing Windows records. Ordinary native jobs use offline bundled indicators.
  Advanced terminal menus, encrypted-backup prompts, dependency/YARA setup,
  acquisition and feed updates remain execution-HELD pending managed adapters.
  Advanced toolkit options links the full official pinned release for review
  and standalone setup; it must not imply those workflows already run natively.
- Every tool job has private temporary paths, exact process/native job custody,
  bounded managed output and validated reports. Default working/report budgets
  are 256 MiB / 64 MiB, with at most eight report sets. Cooperating Python copies and
  writes are bounded; native writers are monitored, not an OS filesystem quota.
  Scan admission needs 3 GiB free plus its working allowance; preparation needs
  64 MiB free. Optional failures do not block main startup. Revert affects only
  the managed engine and preserves preferences, reports and modified originals.
  Unknown or uncertain data remains explicit; cleanup cannot erase source evidence.
- Spyware Scan schedules independently selected native SpywareGuard and curated
  checks with saved toggles, Above normal/High priority and resource choices.
  High is the ceiling; REALTIME is not used. Copied CPU/RAM/I/O and current
  privilege coverage can be unavailable. The requested 10% routine-background
  pace is cadence intent, not a CPU guarantee. Critical control, heartbeat and
  event intake keep their cadence. Verifying privileges never grants UAC rights.
  Scan presentation defaults to supported full/Entire PC checks with click-only
  scope choices and wheel-safe options. Request-bound per-check counters and
  overall fractions show current task/item, elapsed and measured ETA when
  available. Unknown totals/estimates remain explicit. Toolkit activity text
  and resource usage cannot imply file completion or authority. Preserve exact
  timeout/failure reasons, partial progress and native retirement tracking.
  Per-run budgets preserve saved preferences; longer budgets must reach the
  actual operation constructor. Progress uses bounded latest snapshots, not
  growing file logs. Auxiliary dialogs fit their current work area.
  One controller-owned nonmodal after-action report opens after terminal scan
  publication AND actual worker retirement, including failure and partial
  results. Shared views cannot create duplicate reports; shutdown fences late
  callbacks. External findings retain confirmed=False and no response authority.
  Explicit per-run budgets accept 30..14400 seconds. Saved default300 and
  Config/settings maximum900 remain unchanged. Runtime and CPU-time allowances
  propagate consistently; CPU rate, RAM, disk admission, cancellation and native
  custody retain their controls. Progress budget fields cap at14400; elapsed
  records cap at86400 for retirement, while measured ETA remains independent.
  Active quota polling separately accounts for generated file churn; default
  installed/retained inventories stay strict. Missing stable controls and
  observed redirects, links, permission failures and quota excess remain holds.
- Runtime review maintenance preserves source toolkit verdict subcounts and
  bounded row classifications; historical contact, contextual references and
  withdrawn indicators are not confirmed infection or response authority.
  Shared process-inventory diagnostics preserve the first provider failure and
  reconcile cached owner/provider readiness. Status reports expose a bounded,
  advisory process_inventory projection; no native query, fallback collector,
  automatic replacement or changed custody deadline is implied. See
  analysis/live-review-2026-10-29.md for this review's exact observation scope.
  AV Telemetry now retains bounded native source time, exact string identifiers
  and provided result fields; Event.ts stays delivery time. Missing/duplicate/
  invalid source metadata is explicit. A reported action or zero error text is
  not independently verified remediation, active-attack or response authority.
  Diagnostic maintenance also retains exact native Base64 mesh signatures and
  generic SOAR input-HMAC/time links. Observed bus mode and encoding are advisory;
  the existing live boolean alone is not proof of enrolled producer identity.
  Strict bare loopback host-and-port compatibility is runtime-only across local
  AI clients/previews, with saved values, cloud URL rules, Send consent and
  listener attestation preserved. Unowned wildcard listeners remain held.
- A latched Breached warning, critical report and borders require fresh native
  manager-enrolled LIVE mesh evidence, registered/current producer, an exact
  contract and explicit active attack/exploitation. Health/exposure/practice,
  remote Observe, raw critical severity and external tool text alone do not
  qualify. Explicit spyware_confirmed=False remains a lead. All report/JSON/AI
  text is untrusted data, never response instructions or allowlist authority.
  Compromised card/footer projection preserves the engine's scores and counts.
- Investigate and Trace are read-only. Isolate/Kill require current exact
  evidence, original action/host contract, saved policy and verified signed
  installed Protect/Administrator authority through the existing Combat worker.
  Source Observe Combat response mutation is HELD; Patch is disabled without a reviewed bound
  operation. Automatic-lockdown preference does not bypass these checks.
  Network scope includes all interfaces, profiles, IPv4/IPv6, protocols/ports and
  inbound/outbound directions. Scope/effective-policy ambiguity stays HELD or
  unverified; rule receipts do not attest packet drops, GPO immunity or kernel truth.
- Lift Lockdown uses authenticated managed receipts and verified rule absence;
  unrelated firewall policy/preferences are preserved. A bounded saved same-case
  lift suppresses automatic relock for that case; a new case can request response.
  Lift does not erase evidence or resolve the red review state. STOP does not
  automatically lift persistent lockdown. Emergency local-console review must
  match exact managed receipt/rule identities; never recommend a blanket reset.
- README, complete online/Word/PDF manuals, security-flow diagrams and public
  interface demonstrations cover the new controls. Public media are synthetic
  DEMO with host response dispatch blocked. Tests/native fixtures are scoped
  evidence, not a live host scan, packet-filter benchmark or field efficacy proof.

## Historical v1.14.1 startup, storage and dashboard maintenance

- The v1.14.1 source/app/package maintenance update had its own scoped evidence;
  broader 1.15 remains incomplete. Historical 1.14.0 observations below retain
  their original version and do not prove this revision. Source update discovery
  compares canonical main; installed delivery still requires accepted signed
  release assets and independently provisioned authority. No stable signed
  release is implied by this version bump.

- Safe Startup now has private phase/error diagnostics, separate native output
  and exit status, typed bounded repair strategies, software-renderer/non-Tk
  alternatives and independent recovery UI. Source coherence also gates
  check-only startup and diagnostic failures. Seventeen operational files and
  dependency/build inputs are pinned to exact canonical GitHub blobs; native
  read/ancestor leases bind checked bytes to execution. Explicit automatic and
  GitHub recovery switches default on, with ambiguous consent off. Preserved
  source edits can be kept or scheduled for a later startup, never hot-swapped
  into an active engine. Ready snapshots are source-digest bound and do not
  establish a security baseline or response authority.
- Launcher/probe/capture exceptions use a separate infrastructure hold rather
  than selecting application rollback. PowerShell environment values cross the
  strict capture boundary as validated string bases in a typed dictionary.
  Per-attempt diagnostics retain prior failures without attaching their text to
  a later successful attempt. Native directory moves bind expected identities,
  refuse overwrite and retain safe rollback after the forward budget expires.
- Dashboard panels can minimize individually and start open except Module
  health & activity. Responsive budgets retain readable evidence tables and
  resource summaries. Filters/Columns and full row details expose additional
  fields; styled native-font widths keep time/status/header text readable.
- The compact footer EKG uses copied memory publications only. A fresh real
  component heartbeat animates; absent, stale or unavailable evidence flatlines
  red. Details retain exact generations, ages and reasons. This is liveness,
  not attested detector coverage, response authority or a security baseline.
  Live detail refreshes preserve the reader's selection and scroll position.
- Corrected inherited-environment handling restores the supervisor's sidecar
  launch route without permitting credentials, proxies or Python path controls.
  Ensure-Angerona-Recovery.bat supports a read-only check or bounded requests
  through existing authenticated restart inboxes. It honors STOP, disabled Black
  Box and exact core/peer generations; it creates no competing manager. See
  docs/resilience-recovery.md. An inhibited source launch request is not readiness.
- STOP and tray Quit persist authenticated operator intent before AI/startup
  fences and owned-process teardown. Automatic recovery and modern sign-in
  routes honor it. Explicit source startup resumes once after preflight; child
  construction cannot clear a newer STOP. Owned Windows jobs and retained native
  process generations protect shared runtimes. Configured model residency is
  unloaded; shared Ollama daemons and downloaded weights remain. POSIX process
  tree behavior and existing signed binaries were not verified by this work.
- Recovery storage has separate admission budgets and free-space reserves.
  Ordinary source startup uses at most eight fixed critical workspaces, with
  32 MiB/128-entry flat admission and bounded launcher output. Retained
  startup-history counts and recommended reserves become visible advisories;
  actual private write/read and native read-lease custody still apply. Known
  disposable working outputs can be reused after exclusive admission; unknown
  files and existing recovery evidence are preserved. Inherited guards remain
  retained by probes and the launched core. Optional diagnostic output is
  bounded and excess bytes are counted without terminating an active core.
  These are cooperating writer limits, not a filesystem quota on general
  runtime temporary files or a lifetime quota on direct dashboard stdout.
  Source update staging admits two retained candidates with a 2 GiB logical
  aggregate ceiling and 2 GiB volume reserve, under its existing shared lease.
  Unknown or unsafe entries hold admission; no prior candidate is auto-deleted.
  Runtime repair preserves one prior environment, bounds retained transactions
  and requires 5 GiB available before staging. Owned disposable commands retain
  native job custody and monitor a 2 GiB working/log-volume reserve. Pip installs
  avoid eager bytecode compilation and remain hash-locked/offline with bounded
  command and transaction deadlines. An active shared runtime holds replacement;
  unrelated diagnostic processes are not terminated to force a repair.
- The prepared MSIX entry is independent .NET SafeStart, with a fixed helper
  pin, retained process identity, timeout preservation and synchronized close.
  Authenticated modern/legacy selection covers autostart and approved upgrade
  launch; live SafeStart processes hold upgrades. Staged native validation uses
  only the authenticated catalog reconstruction, after threshold authorization.
  Final helper signing must precede pin embedding and final release evidence.
  The external release authority remains unprovisioned; source publication is
  not a signed package release. See docs/enterprise/RELEASE_SIGNING_BOUNDARY.md.
- The 76-page master manual includes security flowcharts, all 86 source module
  entries and a code/test/attack-surface map. README and Welcome/Help explain
  source Observe, installed authority, default public recovery requests and
  Ring 3 limitations. The 45-second real-UI GIF uses synthetic data and blocked
  network/process dispatch. Scoped gates and live observation are recorded in
  analysis/startup-storage-recovery-2026-10-28.md. Direct dashboard stdout and
  general evidence are not covered by a universal drive quota; preserve those
  limitations and coverage gaps rather than claiming every writer is bounded.
- Storage maintenance adds a default 2 GiB total Shadow Shield cache ceiling
  and 2 GiB free-space reserve. Bounded restart accounting and explicit holds
  preserve existing recovery points. Settings > System exposes limits and
  block/delete/change choices, with asynchronous volume warnings and separate
  destructive confirmation. Automatic VSS requests now default off; Windows
  shadow-storage allocation remains independent. No broad temp/evidence purge
  or Windows shadow deletion is authorized by these controls. See
  docs/storage-management.md for scope, coverage and cleanup limits. Initial
  storage gate: 192 passed/six platform or privilege skips/native exit 0,
  unchanged scoped sources and four retained owned process handles retired.
  Data and temporary volumes are sampled off Qt; this is not a total-drive
  quota or live-host protection claim.
- Read-only recovery copies and interrupted staging files need deletion access,
  not content-write access. Cache-only retained handles now retire these exact
  artifacts without attribute rewrites; unsupported operations preserve them.
  Six-version pruning and owned temporary retirement use the same identity-bound
  path. Explicit cleanup continues bounded progress-making passes and reports
  cumulative progress plus complete/incomplete results; no broad purge was added.
  I/O custody releases between passes while copying stays held, allowing primary
  policy/observation progress with explicit limited maintenance coverage. Final
  integration: 218 passed/seven platform or privilege skips/native exit 0,
  unchanged scoped source and five retained owned process handles retired.
## Historical v1.14.0 maintenance evidence

The following observations and former current-state statements describe their
original v1.14.0 revisions. They remain evidence and limitations, not fresh
validation of the current maintained build.

- Continuing GUI stalls exposed a shared process-inventory native call holding
  Python's execution lock. Embedded GUI and direct headless entries now register
  an owned, asynchronous inventory child before readers/modules. Qt refuses admission
  before the cache lock; authenticated bounded observations retain existing
  rich collection, identity checks and collection-start TTL. Failure stays an
  explicit gap, never local native fallback. Windows private job lifetime and
  exact-generation retirement cover child/venv/owned-console processes.
- Authenticated originals proved SpywareGuard promoted a timing-only beacon
  observation into actual termination. Missing, unknown or alert-only beacon
  policy now remains exposure without process, peer or host authority. The
  producer's explicit corroborated policy retains automatic response and
  existing upstream response ownership. No vendor allowlist or baseline reset.
- Live review also proved two real native terminations of another isolated
  checker's inert probes from unleased Purple marker text. Unleased process and
  file markers now remain HIGH observations without response contracts, attack
  classification or copied drill lineage. Bounded observation dedup preserves
  later issuer-attested hits; supported practice response retains live issuer
  authority and independent native evidence. Do not restore marker-text trust.
- Fresh 300-second observations recorded both Chill and Full workloads. The
  final Full window held all 34 scoped runtime hashes unchanged and all 61
  status samples fresh, Full and ARMED. Core CPU was 91.073% of one logical CPU,
  the collector 56.891%, and Black Box 1.000%; collection cost remains material.
  Core window probes had six brief timeouts; Black Box answered all 61. GUI
  heartbeat lag peaked at 625 ms, with no new watchdog entry. These probes do
  not establish alert-detail click latency or isolate a causal speedup.

  reviewed SpywareGuard findings observational. The journal showed no new

## PRODUCT CONTRACT

Angerona is a local-first defensive EDR/NDR/SOAR and digital-forensics
workbench with safe ATT&CK validation and a local Ollama assistant. It is for
home labs, defensive research, learning, purple-team practice, and
security-engineering portfolios.

It is not an independently certified commercial EDR/XDR product. It does not
claim complete attack coverage, state/agency attribution, fleet parity, router
or firmware control, tamper-proof user-mode evidence, or externally validated
efficacy.

No offensive payload, exploit, credential theft, evasion, remote scan,
persistence, attack infrastructure, hack-back, log deletion, arbitrary
response shell, downloaded executable skill, unverified model, or unsigned
kernel component is a product capability.

  scoped positive/negative detection tests and postcondition-verified responses.
  Expiry, loss, stop, replacement and clock discontinuity withdraw proof.
- UGCAP's opt-in witness uses separately enrolled Ed25519 roles and pinned
  private mTLS, explicit create-only initialization and retained signed heads.
  Full witness-appliance rollback still needs a further independent floor.
  Navigate UGCAP > Independent Witness. The private-PKI/mTLS endpoint ends
  /v1/ugcap-witness and needs an exact TLS certificate pin plus witness
  Ed25519 PUBLIC PEM, separate host/witness signing roles and explicit enrollment.
  Applying settings clears cached assurance: attach the vault, enter its
  passcode and satisfy the required TPM-backed hardware challenge, then run
  complete UGCAP Verify now to create a fresh checkpoint. Check witness now
  only heartbeats an already verified checkpoint; it cannot initialize/reset
  the remote head or replace full verification.
  Intentional vault/baseline identity changes require independently reviewed
  witness enrollment or reconciliation. Preserve retained heads/evidence;
  disabling the required witness or deleting/resetting its state cannot make
  changed source trustworthy. No external witness is deployed by this update.
- Authenticated approval seams require real enrolled issuer/subject/key proofs
  over exact operation digests; aliases cannot count as independent operators.
  Durable revocations and outcome verification apply to registered typed
  operations; remaining critical-change wiring is an explicit acceptance task.
- Identity Session Guard has separate opt-in Windows Security event and
  Chromium manifest metadata collectors. Disabled inputs perform no collection;
  denied/retention/replay/unsupported sources remain gaps. No credential values,
  cookies, history or page contents are collected. Manifest grants are unproven.
- Adaptation > Independent Recovery requires a running Immutable Recovery
  Assurance Guard and no UGCAP workspace hold. Enroll an independently trusted
  32-byte Ed25519 PUBLIC key as base64, then explicitly select local ciphertext
  and its signed copy statement. Original 32-byte encryption/audit keys or
  existing protected OS-store keys are required; no keys are autogenerated and
  one-shot keys are never retained for recurrence. At most 16 private decrypted
  test directories are retained without automatic deletion. Opt-in recurrence
  is 1..720 hours, requires reusable protected keys and resets on worker/process
  stop. The signed archive revision is an authority's association; the local
  proof covers selected-inventory extraction and reread, not full Git/system
  reconstruction. Independent backup administration/custody is not deployed.
- tools/evaluate_detections.py --training-cohort PATH checks exact payload
  separation from declared training and package fixtures. Reports retain false
  positives and misses; label independence and undeclared training are unproven.
- AI/tool discovery and connection guide: docs/live-debug-harness.md. Opt-in
  Live Debug exposes a read-only local Windows named pipe for live EventBus
  events and selected diagnostic copies. Under Settings > General > Live AI
  debug and evidence review, enable same-user sharing and restart, or use the
  source launch flag --live-debug. No external
  AI provider, provider SDK or API key is required.
- tools/live_debug.py --pid N reads a finite JSONL snapshot; add --follow for
  live records, --birth FLOAT for independent process creation-time checking,
  --duration 60 for a bounded observation, or --output PATH --max-mib 8
  --backups 3 for capture rotation in an existing parent directory. Local
  --annotate SEQ --verdict threat|false-positive|needs-review --note TEXT emits
  an advisory annotation, never an instruction back to Angerona. Black
  Box has a separate Live AI Review tab. Confirm the actual Angerona process.
  --duration bounds follow mode; a finite snapshot must reach its declared
  retained cursor or report its separate incomplete-snapshot deadline.
- tools/summarize_live_debug.py CAPTURE.jsonl --output NEW.json builds an
  offline issue map for an AI reviewer, including explicit gaps, coverage and
  unverified notes. See the guide for rotation ordering, budget limits and
  target-view digest binding. Case labels never change live protection.
- Component dependencies, interference paths, open causes and the staged
  individual/scanner-only/combined matrix are recorded in
  analysis/live-debug-2026-10-22/interaction-map.md and its issue register.
- SpywareGuard opens one dedicated window from the wider top-right black-spy
  button; it no longer occupies an evidence tab. Header button widths adapt to
  the dashboard. Dated reference briefs remain visible offline; official live
  news requires the existing network opt-in. Headlines have cached details.
- The Modules window's Turn all on action uses background governed admission,
  first-cycle pacing and explicit progress/held/skipped results. It preserves
  platform, consent, Chill, shutdown and UGCAP gates and never flips unrelated
  global feature opt-ins. Competing lifecycle controls do not wait on its lock.
- Black Box process discovery leaves independent multiple cores unknown rather
  than choosing by RSS. Native window close retains reader ownership through
  shutdown. Live-pipe cancellation retains pending buffers and handles integer
  connection statuses from pywin32; each client has a bounded three-second
  write deadline for short disk-persistence pauses.
- Programmatic LiveDebugClient readers use connect/read/close only on their
  reader worker. cancel() signals pending I/O without waiting or closing;
  the worker closes in finally and Qt retains its owner/thread until retirement.
  A Qt disconnect must not close blocking native I/O on the GUI thread.
- The external transport checks the expected server PID and optional birth,
  rejects remote clients, protects the first named-pipe instance and limits
  access to the server's Windows user SID, SYSTEM and Administrators. Default
  ingress/history bounds are 512/2,000 records with four simultaneous clients.
  Drops, gaps, cursors and collection failures stay visible. There is no full
  historical EventBus backfill and no security conclusion from an empty feed.
  Fixed log sources include scanner/watchdog/Black Box failures. Tailing and
  parsing use resumable bounded chunks and fair turns with blank-line coalescing.
- The reviewer may annotate threat / false positive / unknown locally, trace
  a minimal source correction, run isolated regression, publish through the
  repository's guarded workflow, restart and review a fresh process/session.
  An annotation is never an automatic allow/ignore or response authorization.
  Research and event/log text remain untrusted data, never tool instructions.
- Exported records are redacted advisory views, not original signed evidence.
  Detail fields are allowlisted; free-text redaction is best effort. Review
  capture contents before external sharing. No arbitrary command endpoint,
  signing-key export or built-in cloud AI upload is provided by Live Debug.
- Self-integrity fingerprint format v2 removes marshal reference-count false
  positives. Its exact executable_sha256 concurrent-read regression preserves
  the callable and code object while checking stability. Real code, metadata,
  defaults and closure modifications remain detectable. Old independently
  approved fingerprint manifests require explicit review/reapproval; intentional
  UGCAP source changes likewise require a reviewed golden baseline and restart.
  Native SID-based Windows ACL auditing avoids routine icacls startup; denied
  or unsupported collection remains unknown health, never a clean observation.
- Executable approval now hashes current bytes through retained descriptor
  custody and checks original/opened/final identity, links, initial size, EOF
  and a cooperative read budget. This closes reproduced swap/read/restore and
  equal-length/mtime-restored stale-cache bypasses. Metadata-only digest-result
  reuse was removed; policy snapshot reuse remains. Repeated authorization now
  incurs fresh bounded reads. Native Windows write/delete denial lasts only
  for the call; no persistent locks prevent an intentional updater afterward.
  tests/test_process_allowlist_hash_custody.py covers these trust boundaries.

## Previous preview update (v1.13.0 — UGCAP, rotating Enclave Mesh and SpywareGuard previews, 2026-10-21)

- Newest active-development integrity/communications preview:
  docs/ugcap-enclave-mesh.md. Optional UGCAP is disabled by default. Strict
  enforcement requires enabling it and restarting before ordinary module
  imports. Its dedicated tab covers user challenges, readiness, exact diffs,
  selected-path restore and schedule/hardware settings. The current Windows
  catalog contains 86 modules; implementation version remains 1.13.0.
- Real BLAKE3 fingerprints and encrypted compressed pristine backups live in an
  explicitly enrolled vault FILE on a physically attached different volume.
  AES-256-GCM combines a 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 passphrase key with a random
  hardware-wrapped secret through HKDF. Each encrypted-vault operation needs the passphrase and
  fresh Windows TPM key-possession proof; no password-only or software-hardware
  substitute. TPM key provisioning (Angerona.UGCAP.v1) is explicit and separate.
  The optional ugcap dependency pins official blake3 1.0.11 on Python >=3.11 and
  1.0.8 on Python 3.10; both use BLAKE3, with no alternate-hash fallback.
- Opt-in Enclave Mesh gives enrolled producers and handlers ephemeral
  certificates, signed AES-GCM local frames and fresh X25519 exchange every ten
  seconds, with HKDF, counters and replay/expiry checks. Isolated UGCAP uses an
  independently authenticated private worker pipe; UGCAP and Adversary Combat
  control remain available while general mesh traffic is frozen. Successful
  complete verification supplies a source receipt for exact fresh imports and
  communication enrollment; changed source is never accepted by silent TOFU.
- Scheduled challenges default to 168 hours (1..8760 configurable); they ask the
  user to attach media and re-enter the challenge, not decrypt automatically.
  Drift holds managed workers and can request local-host isolation through the
  independent Adversary Combat response policy. Pauses are cooperative and
  in-flight calls are bounded, not atomic revocation of every process/socket.
  Source restore requires a new process and verification; binaries, POSIX
  modified targets and missing-parent paths require offline recovery. Windows
  retained displaced originals stay private; nothing restarts automatically.
- Enclave is a local protocol name, not an impenetrable hardware enclave.
  Externally trusted bootstrap/libraries remain the TCB. Frozen or sourceless
  builds need a separate signed-build receipt and otherwise cannot establish
  this source proof. A vTPM can be cloned; local key continuity is not remote
  attestation. No YubiKey backend. Python wiping is best effort; mounted media
  remain kernel-visible; encrypted audit chains need an independent witness to
  establish rollback resistance. See the guide for exact scopes and limits.

- Newest feature under active development: docs/spyware-guard.md. The dedicated
  SpywareGuard tab exposes recent detections/response receipts, settings,
  reviewed report-URL ingestion, inactive YARA/Sigma/NDR candidates, inert
  sandbox, sourced worldwide surveillanceware profiles and dated news.
  One eligible local rule requests containment; an unbound local finding can
  request local-host isolation under Adversary Combat policy. Research text,
  CVEs, unreviewed indicators, remote records and drills confer no authority.
  SpywareGuard brought the catalog to 85 before UGCAP added the 86th module;
  version remains 1.13.0.
- Optional emergency beacons use authorized existing channel/Signal destinations
  and an independent authenticated liveness watcher. Delivery is best effort;
  power/network loss and containment can prevent it. No development live send.
  AES-GCM forensic archives are encrypted copies; plaintext combat quarantine
  remains. No claim of kernel interception, universal zero-day prevention,
  mobile spyware detection or complete actor/country attribution.
- Users may edit MIT-licensed source, add sensors/rules and improve their own
  posture; docs/writing-modules.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain extension.
  Intentional edits require a reviewed new UGCAP baseline, never blind approval
  of changed code. README includes an actual SpywareGuard UI screenshot with
  explicit DEMO data: docs/screenshots/angerona-spywareguard-preview.png.
- Button path reviews: docs/adaptation-button-review.md and
  docs/selftest-redteam-button-review.md. Adaptation's injected five-probe
  benchmark median was 101.768->23.554ms (4.321x), with a slower cold parallel
  sample. Red Team's measured PID-count operation was approximately 34x faster
  on its test host. Neither measures full-PC speed or live spyware efficacy.
  The button review's 28-phase/85-module selfcheck predates UGCAP; historical
  validation counts below remain evidence for their dated source boundaries.

## Previous maintenance (v1.13.0 — Startup repair and validation, 2026-10-21)

- Source automatic repair: docs/safe-startup.md and
  analysis/startup-repair-2026-10-21/README.md. A fixed supervisor handles only
  recognized runtime/dependency/Tk/Qt outcomes, invokes the repair tool once,
  independently verifies the candidate at its final path and repeats all
  startup checks. Both checkout and canonical helper leases exclude concurrent
  startup. Durable private identities precede renames; interrupted promotion
  must reconcile before any environment process executes. Ambiguous evidence,
  trust failure, low persistent storage, cancellation and live dashboard
  timeout cannot trigger a repair loop. Settings/evidence are preserved; no
  AI/model tools or Chill unlock. Packaged installs retain installer repair.

  native/session/SystemExit zero, completed unconfigure, both atexit markers,

  37-positive-closure and independent OS-witness assertions each.

  subchecks (528 PASS/30 SKIP), nine independent verifiers all PASS. Earlier
  Full-profile diagnostics correctly refused an existing wildcard Ollama

## Chill efficiency and local AI lock (2026-10-18)

- Record: analysis/chill-efficiency-2026-10-18/README.md; instructions:
  docs/hardware-and-selfcheck.md#chill-mode. Version remains 1.13.0.
- Quiet Chill dashboard ticks are 15/30/60s foreground/background/hidden.
  Optional views have 15/30s floors; cosmetic timers and the FPS sampler stop.
  Optional batches receive bounded 50ms cooperative pauses even without pressure.
  Live streaming, event admission, threat wake and watchdog cadence are retained.
- Ollama/Llama startup, inference, streaming, embedding and model-management
  requests stay blocked until manual Full, INCLUDING CHILL: ALERT. Automatic
  escalation never clears the operator AI lock. Only narrow resident-release
  traffic is allowed; retained Angerona-owned daemon handles are stopped after
  model release. Unowned/shared daemons are not killed or globally controlled.
- Automatic core recovery forces Chill, including stale Full commands held by
  an already-running watchdog. Local AI after recovery requires manual Full.
- HEAL retains pending AI diagnosis; TUNE optional learning polls every 64s.
  Recorder empty waits are 5s and replay checks 30s in quiet Chill; arrivals
  immediately wake queues and preserve the original 100ms first-item batch flush.
- Offline policy, GUI callback, recorder and model-lock fixtures do not prove
  physical CPU/RAM savings, native GPU runner exit or long-session stability.

## Hardware adaptation and verified self-check (2026-10-18)

- Record: analysis/hardware-adaptation-2026-10-18/README.md. Operator guide:
  docs/hardware-and-selfcheck.md. Maintenance version remains 1.13.0.
- The shared routine pacer accepts RAM use and available-byte observations
  from Adaptive Resource Governor's existing sampler, including headless engines.
  Invalid samples do not replace a valid lease. Only opted-in routine work is paced;
  streaming delivery, response actions and watchdogs retain their cadence.
- PresentationTimer suspends selected view/animation timers while hidden or
  minimized and adapts visible intervals under pressure. Explicitly stopped timers
  stay stopped. AsyncSnapshot backs blocked-read polling off to 250ms, separately
  from view visibility and job completion. No extra sampling thread is created.
- EntropyWorker blocks for its first input instead of idle 20ms polling. NumPy
  entropy uses a fixed byte histogram; the optional dependency is not required.
  PerfGovernor retains the Process object needed for real CPU delta samples.
- Self-test adds per-module contract checks, strict result validation, timings,
  bounded resource-aware workers, structured evidence with readback, controlled
  failure canaries and inventory/count reconciliation. Skips do not prove readiness;
  absent optional kernel protection is a skip, arbitrary kernel errors are failures.
- The source inventory covers every module and GUI source file. Static call sites
  are not runtime coverage. Virtual CPU/RAM profiles and measured components do
  not prove whole-host speed, native detection efficacy or prolonged stability.

  Detail exports identify their last captured snapshot rather than implying live data.

  and one coalesced follow-up; manager lifecycle locking and explicit settings
  reconciliation remain intact. Blocking lifecycle work no longer occupies Qt.

  start barrier, preventing lock reacquisition from admitting later modules.

  lowercase payload for binary response classification. Freshness, cancellation,
  signature requirements, cursor fairness and scan intervals remain enforced.
- Memory Time-Machine queries TCP only on Windows, where psutil omits UDP peers;
  POSIX retains inet and connected UDP evidence. Unknown listeners no longer
  trigger per-PID rescans; missing remote ownership or failed bulk reads still do.
  Collector gaps remain visible.
- Footer pace near 12% represents an 8x requested routine interval, not CPU use
  or measured throughput. Healthy feedback restores it over at least 24 seconds.
  Measurements are component fixtures, not a universal hardware performance claim.
- Lower pace now also yields active routine work by elapsed time, alongside
  existing item-count pauses. Per-worker timing survives nested counters and
  excludes ordinary cadence sleeps; actual waits extend watchdog deadlines
  without claiming readiness. Scan Center keeps its wall deadline and memory
  traversal retains its separate cumulative rest allowance. Native calls cannot
  be preempted; the standalone real-time telemetry scanner retains its cadence.
