## PRIOR (v1.13.0 — 2026-09-23 improvement loop)

- Canonical upgrade record: analysis/upgrade-20260923/README.md; commands and
  scope: analysis/upgrade-20260923/usage.md; validation and uncompleted gates:
  analysis/upgrade-20260923/validation.md. Version remains 1.13.0. Read-only
  inventory verifies 84 identities, 9 native contracts and 75 compatibility
  adapters; all implementation labels are 1.13.0. Platform declarations cover
  81 Windows, 20 Linux and 19 macOS entries within this shared catalog; these
  are not simultaneous running counts or equally capable enforcement paths.
- Real YARA-X scans now emit typed positive evidence and observed outer-file
  digests. The live Combat worker can automatically quarantine eligible files
  under configured policy, record signed verified results, and support Undo.
  Native inert plain-file/ZIP tests exercised scan to worker to quarantine
  without Ollama or manual action dispatch; changed content is rejected.
- Shark previously omitted its native-producer verifier even when authenticated
  detections existed. The repaired path requires the exact registered built-in
  YARA producer, current manager/bus/recorder graph and lifecycle, plus the
  producer's bounded immutable event receipt. Fabricated signed fields are
  insufficient. Red Team retains its separate validation lease. Receipt expiry,
  eviction or restart can leave historical native proof unavailable. An inert
  BYOVD signature exercises scanning; it never loads a vulnerable driver.
- Bounded ZIP preflight checks the central directory before Python allocates
  its member list. A partial, malformed or over-budget archive retains verified
  positive findings while reporting incomplete coverage and declining a clean
  cache entry. Windows path/descriptor ctime disagreement was repaired using
  a held-handle change token, including restored-mtime regression coverage.
- Shared rich process snapshots preserve immutable rows, collection loss and
  PID birth identity. Three-consumer component timing fell from 314.210 to
  99.543 ms (68.32%). An unchanged-file YARA fixture of 48 files / 6.72 MB fell
  from median 2556.949 to 66.532 ms under concurrent offline tests. Neither
  result establishes whole-PC CPU savings or 24-hour/7-day stability.
- Runtime-alert diagnostics now use a bounded background writer, 4 MiB active
  rotation and fair bounded archive cleanup. Defaults: enabled, 30 days,
  256 MiB; settings allow 1–3650 days and 8–16384 MiB in System and first-run
  setup. Only managed closed runtime_alerts segments are eligible. A sibling
  .keep pins an archive. Active/pinned/inaccessible files can exceed the target;
  pressure/loss remain visible. Signed evidence, pending delivery, action and
  recovery journals, cases, exports and arbitrary data files are excluded.
- Opt-in `python -m angerona --engine-console` connects to a separate ordinary-
  user engine; closing the console does not stop it. Bounded authenticated local
  IPC exposes readiness, events, queued module/Chill/settings operations and
  explicit stop. Event pages account for encoded bytes, including non-BMP text.
  tools/manage_engine.py supplies explicit per-user Task Scheduler, launchd and
  systemd setup. This is not deployed privileged SCM protection. Isolated native
  lifecycle acceptance disabled all 84 modules, so it proves process lifetime
  and reconnect behavior rather than active sensor coverage.
- tools/manage_agent_integrity.py explicitly enrolls exact instruction, memory
  and tool-definition file digests. Integrated Assistant/broker calls and
  Counter-Agentic monitoring enforce the configured boundary. Live-store
  generation floors reject same-session signed-baseline rollback; Windows
  alias checks and held file custody protect approved bytes during mapped
  actions. POSIX mapped mutations are withheld without immutable input custody.
  External agents and kernel socket egress are not thereby controlled; the
  existing process-egress guard remains observe-only.
- tools/run_recovery_drill.py uses actual AES-GCM backup/restore into a new
  private directory, verifies hashes, and retains authenticated drill evidence.
  A native three-file / 1107-byte fixture passed in 6.485 s, including second-
  process verification through the Windows protected key store and tamper
  rejection. Same-host recovery is not independent/offline/offsite protection.
- tools/evaluate_detections.py replays labelled cohorts against verified rule
  packages, reports true/false positives and negatives, and supports explicit
  quality thresholds. examples/cohorts supplies inert synthetic fixtures.
  It executes no attacks; incomplete cohorts withhold quality claims.
- Runtime resource evidence now follows owned process trees and explicit extra
  PIDs. Optional ANGERONA_RUNTIME_METRICS=1 publishes bounded real queue/GUI
  measurements; tools/run_soak.py also accepts authenticated engine metrics.
  PID birth and freshness are checked; headless GUI latency is not applicable.
  Short plumbing tests are not long-duration acceptance.
- Final serial suite after code freeze: 4303 passed / 20 skipped / 0 failed in
  478.73 seconds (7:58), exit 0. Current validation is recorded in the linked
  upgrade document; focused groups overlap and are never added into that total.
  Isolated
  selfcheck: 26 phases passed; SelfTestRunner: 67 passed / 18 prerequisite skips,
  including the separate pipeline test. Selfcheck now stops owned drill workers
  before releasing their validation lease on timeout.
- Pending external gates: publisher signing/notarization credentials, trusted
  privileged Windows deployment, elevated Ollama process acceptance after the
  prior cancelled UAC prompt, native new-service acceptance on Mac/Linux, and
  representative 24-hour/7-day soaks. Prior QEMU Lab and source-launcher native
  evidence remains in the September 23 continuation/deep-review records.
- Proposed/backlog, not shipped: independent backup destination adapters,
  immutable POSIX AI-consumer input adapters, application-scoped native AI
  egress enforcement, expanded native containment matrices and a sensor-demand
  plan. See analysis/upgrade-20260923/comparison.md for priorities and sources.

## LATEST MAINTENANCE (v1.13.0 — 2026-09-23 continuation)

- Canonical record: analysis/continuation-20260923/README.md. Product version
  and catalog count remain v1.13.0 / 84; the Lab backend is not a new sensor.
  Earlier three-round performance measurements and native Mac/Linux CI results
  remain dated evidence in analysis/deep-review-20260923/.
- Analysis Lab now uses a separate fixed-argument QEMU 11.1.0 backend on 64-bit
  Intel/AMD Windows, from a normal non-administrator Angerona session. Pinned
  Bandit 1.9.4 and Gitleaks 8.30.1 analyze copied text without executing it.
  The VMware backend retains its VMX seal and its documented native failure;
  QEMU does not turn that earlier result into a VMware pass.
- Setup is explicit and optional, explains purpose/cost/Skip, and downloads the
  exact reviewed approximately 197 MiB vendor installer when needed. Its normal
  UI, license and UAC prompts remain visible. Keep Program Files\qemu as the
  vendor destination. A matching installation can be reused. A separate
  administrator prompt creates the approximately 122 MiB protected Lab runtime;
  allow 2 GiB free. The vendor certificate is expired, so acquisition explicitly
  relies on reviewed SHA-256/SHA-512 pins, not a currently valid signature.
- The 109-file runtime includes the recursive DLL closure and two firmware
  images. Administrator-owned namespace ACLs, exact hashes/file membership,
  retained directory custody and deny-write/delete leaf seals precede execution.
  Setup independently validates every generated archive member under its seal
  before privileged copying; the elevated helper retains destination ancestry
  itself. It never runs the emulator or guest elevated.
- The fixed diskless profile uses one CPU, 768 MiB guest RAM, single-threaded
  TCG, no NIC/host shares/monitor/user config and explicit firmware. A suspended
  child must pass image/medium-token checks and enter a kill-on-close Job Object
  before resume: one process, 2 GiB process memory, 25% host CPU, below-normal
  priority and at most five minutes per job. No Lab VM is resident while idle.
  Windows host paging/crash dumps still apply; diskless is a guest property.
- Native boot found and fixed Windows QEMU serial burst loss: cbreak is set
  before READY and the exclusive inherited pipe carries one start byte. UUID
  and complete receipt checks remain. The v3 profile disables the unused VAPIC
  option ROM explicitly while retaining ordinary APIC operation. Crypto-library
  configuration/provider overrides block unwanted compiled search defaults.
- Both real analyzer readiness fixtures passed with loopback only, zero block
  devices and no host shares: Bandit B101 in 117.328 s and Gitleaks github-pat in
  62.593 s. The Gitleaks fixture is generated locally and never issued; its
  original alphabetical fixture was legitimately allowlisted. Native loaded
  DLLs came only from the protected runtime or Windows System32/WinSxS. Both
  owned emulator processes were reaped, with none left after the check. Run
  binds readiness to the current catalog and retires stale results on recheck.
- Native elevated Ollama testing reproduced a real Windows linked medium token
  of impersonation type 2. The candidate checks same-user/session/medium
  authority before narrow DuplicateTokenEx conversion, rechecks the resulting
  primary token, and preserves suspended-child verification/no elevated fallback.
  Native token-only controls convert level-2 impersonation but reject level 1
  with ERROR_BAD_IMPERSONATION_LEVEL (1346). This host's actual elevated linked
  token level remains unknown, so the candidate is not an accepted startup fix.
  Focused tests: 146 passed, including two real Windows token-only checks.
  Native process acceptance remains pending after UAC
  cancellation (1223); normal-user startup success is separate prior evidence.
  Automatic authorized defense remains independent of Ollama and the Lab.
- End-to-end native source analysis passed in 47.719 s, with a redacted finding,
  original source-path mapping, saved history and response_authority=False.
  Cancelling a second job reaped its child without extra history; readiness
  remained true. The offscreen GUI displayed the accepted report and history.
- Validation: the first full baseline was 4,103 passed / 19 skipped / 3 stale
  VMware-fixture failures. Final Lab gate: 192 passed, including architecture
  rejection before download and visible-panel setup/Skip refresh; a falsely skipped
  hard-link fixture and its complete six-test file passed after repair. Original
  population reconciliation: 4,107 passed / 18 skips, not another full-suite run.
  The remaining skips are 14 unavailable Windows link-privilege checks and four
  explicit POSIX/native macOS/Linux checks. Compilation covered 393 package and
  56 tool sources; focused Ruff and documentation drift passed. Evidence:
  analysis/continuation-20260923/validation.md. Overlapping gates are not additive.
  QA also fixed trusted PowerShell module-path initialization to precede any
  cmdlet resolution. No cross-platform Lab, arbitrary imported execution,
  host-wide performance claim or AI-authorized response is implied.

## PRIOR MAINTENANCE (2026-09-23 — three review rounds)

- Canonical combined record: analysis/deep-review-20260923/README.md. Product
  remains v1.13.0 with 84 catalog capabilities; no new module-count inflation.
  All 84 entries are accounted for by the final offline inventory: 66 module
  passes, 18 explicit optional/platform skips, plus one event-pipeline pass.
  Existing machine usage excludes unsupported/unused integrations from active
  counts while preserving expected failures and hotplug protection.
- Detection Runtime skips normalization/identity retention when no evaluator is
  configured and bounds cumulative nested-input expansion before serialization.
  Fixture medians: 3,000 idle callbacks 739.411→42.840 ms (94% less); oversized input
  rejection 216.304→0.140 ms and 8,212.1→7.4 KiB peak traced allocation. Ordinary
  configured normalization cost increased about 40 microseconds/event (22%) in
  that run. Shared health provenance reuses identical path resolution (65% less
  fixture time) without extending source-trust cache lifetime. These are
  component benchmarks, not whole-PC or multi-day memory measurements.
- GUI security wake admission spans the complete asynchronous read. In a
  blocked-reader fixture 1,001 Qt wakes become 1; all 1,001 retained serious events
  are classified in 2 reads by the same worker. No new polling timer or worker.
  INFO-only traffic does not start the security reader; failures preserve the
  cursor and teardown refuses late callbacks/results.
- Ollama service preparation is automatic at application launch, AI Triage
  restart and explicit self-test, with asynchronous percentage/stage display.
  Startup validates the exact loopback listener/image and sanitized child
  environment; HTTP and attestation use the same pinned numeric endpoint.
  100% proves service/inventory readiness, not approved model identity or
  inference. No model is downloaded, loaded or approved by startup.
- Native Windows cold start reached 100% in 16.44 seconds with zero resident
  models; warm and Chill service checks also passed. Native testing fixed a
  Windows refusal timeout and stat/fstat timestamp mismatch. Cancellation and
  deadline are rechecked before spawning. macOS/Linux daemon launch remains
  fixture-covered, not natively accepted on this Windows host. POSIX startup
  requires known root-owned images/protected parents; user-owned or symlinked
  Homebrew/application paths may be refused.
- Elevated Windows Protect startup uses only the same user's linked limited
  medium token, checks the suspended child's token/image before resumption,
  and has no administrator fallback. Only validated OLLAMA_MODELS is recovered
  from the user's environment. Inert policy/boundary tests pass; actual elevated
  native process creation remains untested. See ollama-startup.md.
- AI Triage skips narrative requests if telemetry neutralization fails and
  explicitly labels narrative output without response authority. The real
  Combat worker quarantined an inert exact-hash artifact, verified/journaled
  the result and restored exact bytes through Undo with inference unavailable.
  Forged AI/remote/prose claims produced no action. This verifies an existing
  deterministic response boundary, not host-wide detection efficacy.
- Fixed Memory Time-Machine cancellation/ring ownership, Lab final-result queue
  races, semantic-only LSASS/ShadowCopy active-threat assertions, exact-address
  Ollama attestation and ambiguous VMware service paths. Exact dangerous-command
  evidence remains active even when incomplete identity denies response.
- Analysis Lab GUI, pinned Bandit/Gitleaks catalog, appliance preparation,
  bounded supervision and redacted reports/history are implemented. VMX bytes
  and identity stay sealed through supervision/receipt acceptance. Native Lab
  acceptance FAILED on Workstation 25.0.1: VMware cannot open the generated VMX
  under the deny-write/delete seal. Read-only/direct bounded experiments also
  failed. The seal remains; no analyzer receipt was accepted and Run stays gated.
- With explicit user approval, VMAuthdService is now Manual/Running. That solved
  the earlier service prerequisite, not native Lab compatibility. Optional Full
  Setup explains VMware's purpose/cost/Skip, opens Broadcom's account/compliance
  download portal, verifies a user-selected vendor installer and retains its
  custody through interactive UAC, then offers separately confirmed Manual
  service setup. Installation/service startup never grants Lab readiness. A real
  selected VMware 25 installer passed native vendor/product/custody/digest verification;
  the installer itself was not launched.
- macOS 14+ has one source launcher for Intel/Apple Silicon/Rosetta. Intel builds
  pinned cryptography 50 using Xcode/Rust/OpenSSL; it is not a universal binary.
  Linux x86_64 source setup checks Qt libraries and actual bounded offscreen
  QApplication rendering before publishing launchers. New staged runtimes and
  escaped paths preserve working installations on failure. Source-runtime locks
  are complete; older full POSIX release-build locks still have dependency gaps.
- Native Ubuntu, Apple Silicon and Intel CI lanes are configured. Ubuntu source
  installation and offscreen rendering passed after publication; a Mac default-

  and rendering, including Intel's pinned cryptography source build.

  in analysis/deep-review-20260923/publication-followup.md. Visible desktops and

  creation time. Wrappers, unrelated actions and cleanup do not count. Reports
  keep detector-fix contract closure separate and withhold incomplete-run scores.

  startup-checkpoint recovery hold remains separate and was not repaired.

  Busy/failed reads preserve the previous view; actions still recheck authority.

  connection cadence and lexical DNS scores alone are observations. DNS input
  requires typed query fields. Ransomware rename correlation requires changed
  content in the actual renamed files, not unrelated high-entropy media.

  history; Defender continuity failures are health and kernel posture is exposure.

  admission from journal I/O, and rechecks current policy and evidence before action.

  session counters. Combat health and backup exposure do not become active attacks.
- USB prompts use bounded workers, cancellation-safe insertion tokens, one visible
  prompt at a time and no cosmetic reveal delay.

## PRIOR MAINTENANCE (v1.13.0 — Cycle 34 improvement loop)

- Cycle 34 is post-release maintenance, not a version or module-count change.
  Inventory remains 84 Windows-target capabilities: nine native contracts and
  75 compatibility adapters.
- Round 1 fixed five findings (3 High, 1 Medium, 1 Low): broad flow-canvas
  repository serving, a CDN dependency without integrity binding, legacy
  detection-registry governance bypass, detached DetectionForge runtime,
  multi-package live-rule
  eviction, and an unbound Fleet Health Monitor. The canvas is now a
  loopback-only, Host-checked exact allowlist with descriptor/final-path checks,
  bounded fresh metrics, safe text rendering, and an operating-system-selected
  port. AegisPath uses immutable path/node selection indexes.
- DetectionForge now binds one exact live Detection Runtime and complete active
  set. Atomic transaction recovery, nondecreasing authority time, a lifetime
  PID-bound cross-process root-owner lease tied to the immutable registry,
  state, quality, policy, clock, path, and runtime authority, a durable
  governance anchor, and journaled quarantine convergence close downgrade,
  split-brain, crash, stale-runtime, replay, revocation, and stranded-binding
  paths. Published-v2/floorless-v3 migration proves complete authenticated
  history or fails closed.
- Fleet custody v2 authenticates every retained health row and prune boundary.
  Guarded exact-row projections and a generation/SQLite-change-checked cache
  remove the 3N+1 decode/signature path. Clock advance and quota reservations
  commit atomically, exact retry precedes quota, and bounded admission state is
  rebuilt from custody after restart. Retention is 5,000 rows × 8 KiB, about a
  40.96 MB encoded-cache ceiling.
- Registry validation uses a bounded immutable publisher-key snapshot, stable
  package/signature generation proofs, and exit identity/hash checks, closing a
  High key-rotation time-of-check/time-of-use race. Detection Runtime benchmark
  decodes fell 1,920→30 (about 4×); governance reads fell 64→2 (about 2×);
  trust reads fell N→2. Fleet N=250 final mutation was about 0.0188 seconds;
  cached N=5,000 was about 0.289 seconds and deliberate full startup verification
  about 4.475 seconds.
- Current overlapping gates: Cycle 34 targeted 91 passed / 2 expected Windows
  host-capability skips (symlink creation and POSIX fork) / 0 failed; adjacent
  128 passed; package compile
  368/368; standalone self-tests 93 passed / 0 failed plus 16 expected skips;
  supported selfcheck 26/26. The authoritative five-check gate on exact commit
  `7eef1f0a0c400b34f170cbd1463cd3c6a454de3b` passed 2882 / 15 intentional
  platform skips / 0 failed in 977.10 seconds. Canonical evidence-manifest
  SHA-256: `8a6b294ea04157f9232fee5567ac2fb8cb45664cb8f3c74b73c08717ba816d8c`.
  Guarded fast-forward publication carries the validated tree and completion
  record to canonical public `main`.
- Residuals: full detection-root plus local-key rollback needs an independent or
  hardware witness; ambiguous legacy history requires operator recovery; an
  already governed prepublication/work-in-progress root cannot silently mint a
  missing anchor; Fleet is a local lab with conservative post-prune restart
  refill and no remote transport, dispatch, HA, distributed quota authority, or
  production mTLS coordinator.
- Round 1 researched 11 ranked primary-source proposals but retained no exact
  titles and shipped no MVP. The eight Round 3 architecture ideas are all

## PRIOR: v1.12.1 / Cycles 26-30

- Inventory truth: 81 Windows-target built-in capabilities, six native v12
  contracts and 75 explicit compatibility adapters. Every built-in module
  implementation label is 1.12.1; this does not turn compatibility metadata
  into native declarations or claim detection efficacy.
- SentinelLens is a bounded in-memory threat-hunting graph over explicit
  Syslog, Windows Event JSON/JSONL, NetFlow JSON/JSONL, and live EventBus
  evidence. An app-owned background service performs bounded non-blocking
  ingestion, reports queue/parser/analysis loss, and maintains deterministic
  snapshots without delaying sensors. It shows anomaly reasons, exact node
  evidence, and proposal-only remediation. Optional model explanation is
  restricted to a strict loopback endpoint; no cloud fallback or public/LAN
  listening socket is created.
- Guided Auto Adapt combines security-intent choices, complete-evidence gates,
  immutable exact planning, no-write simulation, recovery-baseline custody,
  and separate final approval. The recovery baseline covers complete Windows
  Firewall policy only, not the whole host.
- Every sub-100 module state requires a bounded reason. When provenance is
  provable, Capability Center/Module Inspector show a governed repository path,
  SHA-256 source identity, exact line, public source link, and red read-only line
  highlight. A missing field anchors explicitly to its owning class declaration;
  unavailable or untrusted runtime source is disclosed instead of guessed.
  Unknown, stale, lossy, unsupported, or untrusted evidence cannot be complete.
- Five three-round defensive loops (26-30) reviewed all built-in module files,
  compared primary-source upstream projects, added per-module gates, and used
  repeated independent hostile re-attacks. Tests are inert and temporary; no
  live exploitation, credential collection, persistence, hack-back, or remote
  target scanning is performed.
- Red Team Simulation binds the complete mandatory plan/denominator, exact
  process and detector generations, object custody, native receipts, and the
  signed AAR display/action handoff. The GUI defaults to 38 mandatory stages and
  37 simulation-validation contracts, including 24 fixed inert marker probes;
  native analytic catches remain separately reported. It is not a penetration-
  testing engine and executes none of the named ATT&CK behaviors.
- GitHub CI run 33291595209 passed integrity, audit, and platform-contract jobs
  but failed all four Windows Python matrices on a transient delete-pending
  publication-runtime cleanup race. Security assurance run 33291595229 passed.
  The exact failure and a second timing-dependent authentication-baseline alias
  diagnosis were reproduced locally, fixed with bounded fail-closed object
  custody, and retained as hostile regressions. Final-SHA workflow status is
  verified on GitHub rather than inferred locally.
- A second exact-completion run, CI 33294618414, passed README integrity,
  dependency audit, and all platform contracts but reopened the four Python
  matrices. Security assurance 33294618400 passed. The failures proved that a
  sealed DACL still granted effective write through enabled Administrators
  membership and implicit owner `WRITE_DAC`, while two tests coupled unrelated
  assertions to mutable hosted Git and an elevation mismatch. The DACL now
  omits BA in both states and gives exact OWNER_RIGHTS read/execute while sealed;
  ordinary tests are hermetic, and the real publisher retains its byte-exact
  live profile.
- Terminal release evidence on the exact v1.12.1 tree:
  2678 passed / 13 intentional host-platform skips / 0 failed across 2691
  tests. Completion SHA `45c114b99c0f071fb0c2d13de2a78928a35ee514`
  historically passed Security assurance 33296804422 while CI 33296804448
  reopened WFP and FIM races on Python 3.11/3.13; a local T1059 reattack found
  additional cadence/direct-observation gaps. All are remediated, and guarded
  publication verified remediation release commit
  `f6c5a6da709ef45b9c95bfe700ed3367c2f00675`, canonical public `main`, a clean
  tree, and all 4/4 README images. This terminal record is carried by the

  semver are independent; never call all 80 native v12 implementations.
- Capability Center and Module Inspector search, filter, typed-sort, and open
  bounded details for contracts, source, dependency, permission, path,
  lifecycle, freshness, loss, and recent evidence.

### Guided Auto Adapt and firewall recovery

- Guided Auto Adapt presents closed Balanced, Public, and Emergency Lockdown
  choices. It performs audit, completeness gating, immutable planning, and
  no-write simulation. Accepted choices are copied immutably before background
  work; an optional apply needs a separate confirmation of the exact plan.
- Context automation is proposal-only. Legacy/tampered `auto_apply` state is
  reset false; AI/content/observations do not authorize unattended mutation.
- Recovery baseline enrollment is explicit, HMAC-authenticated, host-bound,
  and non-replaceable. Apply refuses before mutation without a complete
  baseline. The baseline restores complete Windows Firewall policy only—the
  complete mutation scope of Host Adaptation—not hardware, services, ports,
  applications, network devices, or whole-host configuration.
- Every apply has a pre-change snapshot, HMAC transaction journal, exact
  verification, compensation, startup reconciliation, and circuit breaker.
  Fresh bounded WTS, SSH/current-session, and common remote-control agent
  process checks reduce lockout risk; unknown evidence cannot authorize.
- Run safe automatic checkup audits once and simulates all profiles without
  writing.

### Clickable evidence and bounded work

- Shared tables sort typed severity and numeric risk rather than display text.
  Adaptation, alert, Live Defense, Context Info, CVE, capability, module, and
  governed-path rows open bounded read-only details.
- Alert identity, deterministic fingerprint, and verified HMAC authenticity
  are distinct labels. Analysis is bounded to 2 active workers plus 6 queued
  exact event identities with deduplication.
- Exact-rule suppression is confirmed, 15-minute, audited, undoable, and never
  available to integrity alerts. SOAR clear creates an atomic recoverable
  archive/digest manifest and restore refuses overwrite. CVE workers are owned
  and nonblocking.

### Durability, authority, and hardening

- SIEM/Remote use bounded durable outboxes, monotonic revision cursors,
  drain-stage-drain, explicit gap receipts, leases/retry/dead-letter,
  persistent tombstones, and HMAC-authenticated mutable state. The local queue
  key is independent of transport-key rotation.
- Delivery is at least once and may duplicate. Row deletion/whole-database
  rollback is not independently witnessed. Transport-key coordination uses
  restart epochs.
- Settings and Intel Sync use atomic publication; Settings compensates exact
  settings bytes, protected credentials, environment projection, and autostart.
- Evolution, mitigation tuning, contextual adaptation, and unapproved
  behavioral learning are proposal-only. Behavioral activation requires exact
  SHA-256 approval and hash drift returns to pending review.
- Self-integrity covers full callable semantics. Persistence uses explicit
  COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN. Process/driver/direction-specific firewall actions
  bind exact identities, return codes, postconditions, and rollback. Ambiguous
  ACL lockdown is not a production automatic action.
- IPC key custody uses the OS protected store with exact legacy plaintext
  migration/residue removal. IPC Guard is an authenticated loopback diagnostic
  admission preview, not a production payload consumer or TPM-backed channel.

### Standards and upstream comparison

- ATT&CK 19.2 curated endpoint catalog across 15 Enterprise tactics;
  Navigator 5.3.2/layer 4.5; constrained-preview OCSF 1.8 typed resolving
  observables; deliberately limited Sigma subset with atomic bounded
  admission/refusal receipts. These are not complete ATT&CK coverage, OCSF
  compiler, or full Sigma compatibility claims.
- Primary-source comparison used Velociraptor client monitoring/local buffers,
  Wazuh stateful/stateless Active Response, Fleet policy definitions, osquery
  packs/selectors, Elastic detection-as-code validation, and Velociraptor
  community-artifact warnings. Angerona adapted local design lessons; it does
  not claim their fleet/server/content ecosystems or support model.

- Capability summary: 43.324 -> 1.508 us/call (96.5% faster).
- Stable Module Inspector tick: 13.458 -> 0.474 ms (96.5% faster).
- At this historical Cycle 25 cutoff, batched commits, compiled Sigma plans and
  a global detail-worker cap were deferred. v1.14 now has compiled runtime plans,
  atomic exporter batches and application-wide two-detail admission; current row
  freshness/lifetime validation is recorded in the latest checkpoint above.
- Authoritative serial release evidence, including the 3 final-performance
  tests: 1,811 passed / 6 expected host-platform skips / 0 failed. The added
  tests and their surrounding performance/reliability group also passed a
  focused 106/106 gate.
- Compile 346/346; 82/82 module files imported; 64/64 compatibility hooks;
  80 capability discovery; 92 core/module self-tests passed plus EventBus and

## LATEST: v1.11.0 / Cycle 24

### Module and platform facts

- Static platform discovery: 80 Windows modules, 14 Linux modules, 13 macOS
  modules.
- Windows contract: Protect in elevated user mode; no unsigned kernel driver.
- Linux contract: Observe plus optional privileged BCC/eBPF supplement. This is
  not a universally shipped CO-RE kernel sensor.
- macOS contract: Observe preview; no Endpoint Security or Network Extension
  enforcement claim.
- Final converged serial validation: 1,675 collected across 229 files; 1,670
  passed; 5 expected host-capability skips; 0 failed.

### Authenticated evidence and advanced correlation

- `core/sensor_provenance.py` provides strict, bounded,
  producer-authenticated event envelopes with exact schemas, sequence/replay
  state, loss metadata, and consumer constraints. EventBus HMAC protects stored
  bytes; it does not prove in-process producer identity.
- `modules/ssh_surface_guard.py` (SSHG) is observe-only. It inventories
  bounded OpenSSH configuration/Include graphs, configured public-key/CA/
  principals sources, public-key fingerprints and custody, services, listeners,
  fixed-provider authentication evidence, and normalized forwarding.
- SSH live ingestion requires the broker-assigned producer
  `OpenSSH Auth Event Collector`, exact event type, fixed provider/channel/
  message schema, and loss-aware sequence continuity. Rejected consumer schema
  does not consume continuity invisibly.
- SSHG never reads a private key or credential, attempts login, probes a
  listener, opens a tunnel, changes configuration, or retains/publishes full
  commands, full command lines, or raw endpoints.
- `modules/audit_log_guard.py` (ALIG) detects observed clear/tamper identities,
  audit-policy/logging-service changes, continuity/generation gaps, record
  reuse, provider/channel rejection, and authenticated cursor damage. It never
  clears, alters, restores, or reconstructs a Windows log.
- `modules/temporal_tradecraft_correlator.py` (TTCR) performs bounded,
  restart-aware ordered correlation for SSH persistence/session/tunnel,
  network-path drift, and log-clear sequences.
- `modules/identity_session_guard.py` (IDSG) consumes authenticated structured
  identity/session evidence for privacy-tokenized LUID/session, device-code,
  new-device, browser-store, RMM, and privilege-transition analytics. It does
  not acquire credentials, tokens, browser contents, or tenant sessions.

### Platform, driver, peripheral, and recovery posture

- `modules/driver_provenance_guard.py` (DPVG) joins image SHA-256,
  Authenticode/catalog evidence, blocklist disposition, Hypervisor-Protected
  Code Integrity, and Secure Boot. It is read-only; overflow and unknown
  evidence are explicit. On-disk evidence is not claimed as perfect loaded-
  kernel-image identity.
- `modules/platform_attestation_guard.py` (PATG) observes local Secure Boot,
  virtualization-based security, HVCI, boot flags, and TPM presence. Hardware
  attestation is reported only when an injected verifier accepts a fresh
  nonce-bound quote. The default collector does not fabricate one.
- `modules/peripheral_dma_guard.py` (PDMG) observes Kernel DMA/IOMMU,
  Thunderbolt, USB4, removable-storage, and device-install posture. It does not
  control devices or prove device firmware. Linux removable absence is complete
  only when every enumerated flag is a stable no-follow valid zero.
- `modules/immutable_recovery_guard.py` (IRAG) evaluates externally signed
  recovery-copy evidence. Quorums are satisfied inside one exact expected
  revision/archive/manifest cohort; restore tests bind to that cohort.
  Excessive future timestamps, mixed cohorts, unstable/linked evidence, and
  unbounded directories fail closed. No restore is performed.

### Network zero trust and Personal Sentinel

- `modules/network_trust_monitor.py` (NZTR) treats every active physical
  Wi-Fi/Ethernet path as untrusted. Restart-safe privacy tokens represent DNS,
  DHCP, route, gateway, profile, interface generation, and path additions.
- `core/personal_sentinel_gateway.py` is the explicitly enrolled direct-HTTPS
  first-hop client. It requires normal TLS/hostname validation plus a leaf
  certificate pin, nonce/freshness, expected policy digest, optional mTLS,
  complete IPv4/IPv6 selected-route evidence, no proxy/redirect, and unchanged
  pre/post route context.
- `core/personal_sentinel_authority.py` and
  `tools/personal_sentinel_server.py` supply a separately operated reference
  authority/server for mandatory production mTLS, Ed25519 response/state
  signing, trusted-time receipts, and monotonic compare-and-swap evidence.
  Admission is bounded; the state has singleton custody, durable sequence
  floors, and irreversible close semantics.
- Intended topology: Angerona host -> operator-controlled Personal Sentinel
  gateway/firewall -> upstream/ISP router -> Internet.
- Sentinel is not a bundled router/appliance, routing role, management plane,
  remote command service, or firmware attestor. It performs no router
  discovery/configuration, credential storage, route change, firewall mutation,
  or firmware trust. A positive first-hop label grants no endpoint, identity,
  application, destination, or upstream-router trust.
- Operators must independently provision the reference service host,
  certificates, key custody, protected state, enrollment, monitoring, backup,
  and recovery. Local signed/ACL-protected floors do not resist privileged
  whole-host snapshot rollback without a TPM or independent witness.
- `core/process_egress_lease.py` is a process/start/user/destination/path/
  budget policy broker; `modules/process_egress_guard.py` (PELG) observes its
  authenticated audit stream. It is not a firewall. Enforcement requires a
  separately privileged injected adapter and retained OS process/file identity.

### Release trust

- Public Windows first install: signed full-trust x64 MSIX only. Windows must
  validate the MSIX block map and exact provisioned publisher identity before
  activation.
- The release workflow requires an externally configured package name,
  publisher distinguished name, publisher certificate, and protected signing
  environments. The repository does not claim Microsoft Store deployment.
  Enterprise/App Installer policy and clean-VM validation are external gates.
- Classic Inno Setup is non-public, restricted, and prior-approved-install
  migration-only. It performs unelevated preflight and delegates UAC/mutation
  to the protected installed updater. It is not a public release asset or
  first-install bootstrap.
- Portable ZIP install is upgrade-only. The installed native verifier checks
  the exact candidate, payload manifest/catalog, SBOM/provenance digests,
  threshold authorization, enrolled roots, protected ACL custody, and numeric
  release version/sequence floor before target mutation.
- Signer jobs have separate protected environments. A signer response contains
  only signer ID, statement digest, and signature. The finalizer requires the
  exact separately supplied canonical 2-of-2 root policy and protected policy
  SHA-256. Signer artifacts cannot replace authority roots.
- A local protected rollback floor cannot resist privileged restoration of the
  whole host. TPM-backed or independently witnessed monotonic state is needed
  for that attacker model.
- `modules/release_transparency_guard.py` (RTAG) is runtime observe-only
  defense in depth. It is not the first-install trust bootstrap.

### ARIA Defense Memory and RAG provenance

- `assets/angerona_defense_memory.json` is Defense Memory v1.1.0 with 18
  capability, usage, defensive-measure, limit, and actor-neutral tradecraft
  entries.
- `core/defense_memory.py` admits it only after stable non-reparse bounded
  reading, strict duplicate-free schema validation, structural/text limits, and
  canonical digest verification:
  sha256:97a7771a9ce38ac66c6889dc90e0d591b64e07c2f169a0cebd7a57c119d67d57
- Defense Memory is data-only. It defines no tool, action, prompt authority, or
  executable procedure. Local retrieval can use its admitted content. If a
  cloud fallback is separately enabled and authorized, at most one
  highest-ranked canonical Defense Memory excerpt is redacted and eligible.
- `modules/rag_provenance_guard.py` (RAGP) validates explicitly configured,
  root-confined, digest-bound future sources and emits inert taint/trust labels.
  It does not change an index or Defense Memory and needs a caller-owned
  verifier for signed trust tiers.
- Local Ollama remains the default. Model output and retrieved text are
  advisory evidence; they cannot self-authorize a tool or arbitrary PowerShell.

### Live Defense Activity

- `gui/live_defense_activity.py` requests at most 16 recent public EventBus
  records, displays at most five sanitized summaries, and adds coarse module
  health.
- It never reads event details, raw telemetry, source code, executing source,
  hidden AI reasoning, private chain-of-thought, credentials, local paths,
  addresses, SSIDs, or interface identities.
- It is an operational activity surface, not a debugger or reasoning viewer.

## RESPONSE AUTHORITY

Adversary Combat is the governed mutation boundary. Supported exact-target
classes include block exact remote peer, isolate exact executable, suspend or
terminate verified process, quarantine exact file, activate bounded deception,
explicitly isolate host, and undo verified reversible actions.

Contracts bind action, process birth, executable/file identity, peer, lifetime,
sequence, and escalation. Capability state uses durable epoch/high-water
continuity. Durable intents, verified postconditions, signed receipts, exact
Undo, startup recovery, compensation, and mutation circuit breakers make
effects visible and recoverable.

Protected/system targets, stale process identities, path replacement, ambiguous
PowerShell semantics, weak cross-entity correlation, and unsigned or malformed
authority fail closed. Model output, retrieved content, public EventBus text,
and observe-only module findings never grant response authority by themselves.

## ARCHITECTURE

- `src/angerona/core/`: EventBus, provenance, policy, response contracts,
  capability authority, file/process leases, trusted time, Sentinel authority,
  recovery, release authority, ARIA/RAG, evidence, cases, custody, and platform
  abstractions.
- `src/angerona/modules/`: independent BaseModule detectors/responders.
- `src/angerona/gui/`: dashboard, Live Defense Activity, Flow Dashboard /
  Local SOC, operations, Settings, Scan Center, Red Team, ATT&CK, Combat
  history/Undo, ARIA, and Upgrade Console.
- `src/angerona/shark/`: bounded non-destructive simulations and AAR evidence.
- `src/angerona/telemetry/`: bounded process/network snapshots and normalized
  sensor data.
- `tools/`: compile/selfcheck/release/validation helpers and Personal Sentinel
  reference server.
- `analysis/loop/`: red-team, remediation, performance, innovation, and
  verification evidence.

Normal flow:

sensor -> broker-authenticated typed evidence -> HMAC EventBus -> recorder /
correlation -> incident / SOAR -> signed response contract -> Adversary Combat
-> durable intent -> exact action -> verified postcondition -> signed receipt
-> Undo / recovery

## DATA, SECRETS, AND EGRESS

- Source/development data uses the checkout sibling `AngeronaData`.
- Packaged Windows data prefers protected `D:\AngeronaData`, with protected
  `%ProgramData%\Angerona` fallback.
- macOS uses its application-support area; Linux uses XDG state.
- Secrets use Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service when the
  protected backend is required.
- Runtime data, credentials, private signing material, diagnostics, journals,
  models, evidence, and local state are not source artifacts and must not be
  committed.
- Cloud, messaging, SIEM, threat-intelligence, and peer integrations are
  optional and off by default. Any selected data crossing an enabled connector
  remains subject to its separate consent/redaction contract.

## CYCLE 25 FINDING DISPOSITION

- Round 1 recorded 12 traceable risk/reliability lineages without invented
  retrospective CVSS scoring; all are fixed or truthfully scoped.
- Round 2 re-audited 8 overlapping durability/lifecycle records and fixed all
  8, including one IPC self-test concurrent-accounting race.
- Round 3 performed 12 final closure checks and found no open High/Critical code
  finding in the v1.12 change set.
- Accepted boundaries include firewall-only recovery scope, at-least-once
  duplicates, no independent witness for outbox deletion/whole-DB rollback,
  restart-epoch transport-key coordination, constrained OCSF/Sigma, diagnostic-
  only IPC, and 75 compatibility adapters.

See `analysis/loop/cycle25/prior_findings.md` and
`analysis/loop/cycle25/summary.md`.

## CYCLE 24 FINDING DISPOSITION

- Round 1 opened 10 defects plus 1 informational runtime/deployment boundary.
- Round 2 re-audited 7 release/integration/lifecycle issues or residuals.
- All seven Round 2 findings received code remediation and focused regressions.
- Round 3 opened 4 findings (1 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low); all four received code
  or documentation remediation and focused regressions.
- Release first-install trust still requires provisioned Windows publisher and
  deployment policy; release roots/policy still require protected external
  custody; privileged whole-host rollback still requires TPM/independent
  monotonic state.
- Broker keys, trusted-time/high-water state, recovery evidence, and Sentinel
  authority state must live outside a restorable monitored-host snapshot when
  snapshot rollback is in scope.
- Older architectural residuals remain: in-process admitted-extension authority
  (A-04), broad legacy PowerShell policy surface (A-06), and the preferred
  retained OS process/executable-file lease across path-wide firewall mutation
  (R6-03).

See `analysis/loop/cycle24/prior_findings.md` and
`analysis/loop/cycle24/summary.md`.

## PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE

- Cycle 25 recorder handoff: 22.306 to 15.925 us/event (28.6% faster).
- Cycle 25 capability summary: 43.324 to 1.508 us/call (96.5% faster).
- Cycle 25 unchanged Module Inspector tick: 13.458 to 0.474 ms (96.5%
  faster).
- Historical Cycle 25 deferrals: batched commits, compiled Sigma plans and global
  detail admission. Their v1.14 implementations and scoped acceptance are recorded
  above; historical measurements do not validate later row-freshness changes.
- Historical Cycle 24 evidence follows.

- Personal Sentinel canonical unsigned-state reuse: 30.2-39.0% lower measured
  serialization/signing kernel CPU across 64-4096 nonces; fsync/replace
  unchanged.
- Identity replay membership: O(n) to O(1), 410.488 us to 0.060 us at the
  artificial 4096-event bound; authoritative ordered-window semantics retained.
- Bounded directory iteration: 0.0242 ms versus 3.3220 ms in a synthetic
  100,000-row over-budget case and, more importantly, exactly limit+1 rows
  consumed.
- Fixed-schema sensor admission added 4.060 us/event in the synthetic 5,000-
  event benchmark.
- Two complete public-gallery runs produced byte-identical output.
- No optimization relaxed cadence, freshness, cryptography, stable reads,
  completeness, response authority, or fail-closed behavior.

## KNOWN LIMITS / NOT SHIPPED

- No whole-host rollback from the Host Adaptation baseline; it covers complete
  Windows Firewall policy only.
- No exactly-once exporter claim, independent outbox rollback witness, or
  coordinated no-restart transport-key epoch protocol.
- No full OCSF/Sigma implementation or complete ATT&CK coverage claim.
- No IPC production payload consumer or TPM-backed transport.
- No claim that 75 compatibility adapters are native v12 implementations.
- No turnkey Personal Sentinel appliance, router, routing role, router
  credentials, router discovery/configuration, firewall mutation, remote command
  plane, or firmware attestation.
- No automatic process-egress enforcement adapter.
- No default hardware quote provider/verifier or hardware-rooted recovery/
  release high-water.
- No authoritative cloud identity/session collector; IDSG consumes supplied
  structured evidence.
- No claim that on-disk driver bytes perfectly identify a currently loaded
  kernel image.
- No recovery from logs/evidence already deleted before collection.
- No public classic Setup first install and no Microsoft Store deployment claim.
- No independent certification, commercial fleet support, long elevated soak,
  clean-machine publisher matrix, physical sleep/resume matrix, native
  Linux/macOS release acceptance, field false-positive baseline, or independent
  efficacy evaluation.
